content: 1. Co Minh HB, Bousquet PJ, Fontaine C, Kvedariene V, Demoly P conducted a study analyzing risk factors for systemic reactions during skin testing with beta-lactam antibiotics. Their findings were published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology in 2006 (Volume 117, Pages 466–468). 2. Lockey RF, Benedict LM, Turkeltaub PC, and Bukantz SC reported on fatalities associated with immunotherapy and skin testing in their 1987 study published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (Volume 79, Pages 660–677). 3. Nolan RC, Puy R, Deckert K, O’Hehir RE, and Douglass JA evaluated a new commercial skin testing kit for identifying IgE-mediated penicillin allergies. Their findings were published in the Internal Medicine Journal in 2008 (Volume 38, Pages 357–361). 4. Riezzo I, Bello S, Neri M, Turillazzi E, and Fineschi V documented a case of fatal anaphylactic shock related to intradermal ceftriaxone testing, highlighting the medico-legal implications. This case was published in the journal Allergy. 5. Sogn DD, Evans R III, Shepherd GM, Casale TB, Condemi J, Greenberger PA, et al. presented results from a National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases clinical trial assessing the predictive value of skin testing with major and minor penicillin derivatives in hospitalized adults. This study appeared in the Archives of Internal Medicine in 1992 (Volume 152, Issue 5, Pages 1025–1032). 6. Van Dellen RG reviewed the utility of skin testing for penicillin allergy in a 1981 publication in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (Volume 68, Pages 169–170). 7. Blencowe H, Cousens S, Kamb M, Berman S, and Lawn JE explored the impact of syphilis detection and treatment during pregnancy on reducing stillbirths and neonatal mortality. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2011 (Volume 11, Supplement 3, Article S9). 8. Alexander JM, Sheffield JS, Sanchez PJ, Mayfield J, and Wendel GD Jr. assessed the efficacy of syphilis treatment during pregnancy in a study published in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 1999 (Volume 93, Issue 1, Pages 5–8). 9. Chang SN, Chung KY, Lee MG, and Lee JB investigated the seroreversion of syphilis serological tests in newborns born to treated syphilitic mothers. Their findings were published in Genitourinary Medicine in 1995 (Volume 71, Issue 2, Pages 68–70). 10. Donders GGG, Desmyter J, Hooft P, and Dewet GH reported on the apparent failure of a single injection of benzathine penicillin G for syphilis treatment during pregnancy in HIV-seronegative African women. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1997 (Volume 24, Issue 2, Pages 94–101). 11. Klein VR, Cox SM, Mitchell MD, and Wendel GD Jr. described the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction complicating syphilis therapy during pregnancy in a 1990 study published in Obstetrics and Gynecology (Volume 75, Part 1, Pages 375–380). 12. Lu J, Huang C, and Zeng Y reviewed syphilis in pregnant women in a 2001 publication in Zhonghua Fu Chan Ke Za Zhi (Volume 36, Issue 8, Pages 456–459). 13. Mullick S, Beksinska M, and Msomi S evaluated compliance with the three-dose standard treatment regimen for syphilis in antenatal care. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2005 (Volume 81, Issue 3, Pages 220–222). 14. Myer L, Karim SSA, Lombard C, and Wilkinson D studied the effect of multiple doses of benzathine penicillin on pregnancy loss in rural South Africa. This study appeared in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2004 (Volume 9, Issue 11, Pages 1216–1221). 15. Myles TD, Elam G, Park-Hwang E, and Nguyen T examined the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction and fetal monitoring changes in pregnant women. Their findings were published in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 1998 (Volume 92, Issue 5, Pages 859–864). 16. Phaosavasdi S, Snidvongs W, Thasanapradit P, Ungthavorn P, Bhongsvej S, Jongpiputvanich S, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of benzathine penicillin regimens in treating syphilis during pregnancy. This study was published in the Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand in 1989 (Volume 72, Issue 2, Pages 101–108). 17. Watson-Jones D, Gumodoka B, Weiss H, Changalucha J, Todd J, Mugeye K, et al. assessed the effectiveness of antenatal syphilis screening and single-dose benzathine penicillin treatment in preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes in Tanzania. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2002 (Volume 186, Issue 7, Pages 948–957). 18. Stark BJ, Jamison RB, Molina RD, and Sullivan TJ discussed penicillin allergy and desensitization in serious infections during pregnancy in a 1985 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Volume 312, Issue 19, Pages 1229–1232). 19. Zhang XM, Zhang RN, Lin SQ, Chen SX, and Zheng LY conducted a clinical analysis of 192 pregnant women infected with syphilis. This study was published in Zhonghua Fu Chan Ke Za Zhi in 2004 (Volume 39, Issue 10, Pages 682–686). 20. Zhou P, Gu Z, Xu J, Wang X, and Liao K evaluated ceftriaxone as a treatment agent for primary and secondary syphilis during pregnancy. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2005 (Volume 32, Issue 8, Pages 495–498).
